- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is positive (especially > 0.20), model often overreacts — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshooting.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon — add 1.5–3.0% buffer to forecasted peak values.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day avg), model lags by 2–5 days — adjust forecast to anticipate continuation or reversal within next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., ±0.30 or higher), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by 1–2% downward bias.  
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 5 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often fails to capture downward drift — add 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment to forecast.
